take: Middle East chokepoint flows rose 19% in 3Q26, a reminder that supply-route risk premia remain live even as refinery inputs recovered only modestly after the 4.8 million b/d second-quarter collapse, keeping crude differentials and freight insurance costs supported. On the shipping side, Jinhui has re-marketed the supramax Jin Bi at $17.8m versus a failed $14.4m, and Precious Shipping has fixed the ultramax Sarita Naree on an index-linked charter of up to 13 months, signalling firmer dry bulk asset sentiment that feeds through to bunker demand. The product angle is the distillate tilt: refiners have shifted yields away from gasoline towards middle distillates on high jet and diesel margins, yet U.S. refiners still drowned their own gasoline windfall, so watch cracks for oversupply in gasoline versus tightness in distillate. Cross-market, European EV and hybrid registrations at around 75% of new car sales erode the structural gasoline pull, reinforcing the gasoil-over-gasoline spread and, by extension, the bunker complex. In the next 24 hours, watch the December Fed rate-hike expectations flagged for 9 December against the delayed November inflation print, plus any follow-through in dry bulk period fixtures and bunker pricing.
